title: Tenant evidence offer and status micro-update
body:
Purpose
----
Working draft for a short status update to publish on status.redwood.ai plus a customer-facing mini-postmortem and an opt-in evidence/replay offer for affected tenants. Aim: reassure quickly, give verifiable evidence for customers who want to reconcile, and surface clear action choices (replay, accept compensation credit, or manual verification assistance).

Audience
- Primary: enterprise and mid-market tenants impacted by intermittent truncated outputs and elevated 5xx rates (region: us-west-2) on 2026-11-29 03:12–04:35 UTC.
- Secondary: partner integrations, internal SEs and account teams.

Micro statuspage update (short form for status.redwood.ai)
----
Title: Partial degradation of text generation in us-west-2 — mitigation in progress
Summary (one line): We detected and mitigated a partial degradation affecting text generation responses (truncations/5xx) in us-west-2; a subset of requests may have experienced truncated outputs or retries between 03:12–04:35 UTC on 2026-11-29.
Impact: Some tenant requests may have returned truncated text or transient 5xx errors. No customer data was exposed.
Current status: Mitigation applied, traffic routed to fallback pool; monitoring shows success. We are validating full recovery and preparing a customer evidence package.
ETA for next update: 2026-12-02 18:00 UTC or earlier.

Suggested short statuspage body (copy-paste)
----
We observed a serving regression impacting text generation in our us-west-2 region between 2026-11-29 03:12 and 2026-11-29 04:35 UTC. During this window, some requests returned truncated outputs or 5xx errors. Immediate mitigation included routing affected traffic to a stable fallback pool and applying a patch to the routing policy. We are completing verification and will follow up with a customer evidence package for tenants who want replayable logs and integrity checks.

Customer-facing mini-postmortem (plain language)
----
TL;DR: A software regression in request routing caused an incorrect KV cache invalidation that intermittently truncated outputs and returned 5xx errors for a subset of requests. We routed traffic to a verified fallback, rolled out a fix to prevent the cache invalidation, and validated recovery. For customers who want to confirm impact on their data/requests, we offer a tenant evidence package (details below).
What happened (technical, short): A recent change to our multi-pool routing optimizer introduced an edge-case where a prefix cache eviction was triggered for high-concurrency sequences. That eviction produced stale KV pointers for a small percentage of requests, resulting in truncated continuations or internal retry errors.
Scope: Affected tenants: approximately 0.6% of active tenants in us-west-2; request failure/truncation rate for impacted customers peaked at ~12% of their requests during the window.
Root cause: Improper coordination between routing optimizer and KV cache cataclysmic-eviction path when sequence concurrency > 512.
Fix applied: Reverted the optimizer change and deployed a targeted guard in the KV cache layer to abort the unsafe eviction path. We also force-rotated fallback routing for in-flight requests during the mitigation window.
Prevention: Added automated unit+integration tests around cache eviction invariants, and a synthetic workload harvester that exercises concurrency > 512 at staging every deploy.

Evidence and replay offer (tenant-centered)
----
For tenants who want to validate effects on their traffic, we will prepare a tenant evidence package containing: 
- Per-tenant request timeline (timestamps, request-id, model, route taken) in CSV format
- Response fingerprint: first-256-token SHA256 snapshots for before/after (where available)
- Service-side trace links and operator notes for requests that retried or returned 5xx
- Integrity hashes for each artifact and a signed manifest for auditability
Offer details: Customers can opt in to receive the evidence package or request an operator-led replay. Replays will be executed in a controlled, read-only sandbox using recorded inputs and the recovered model state (no data mutation).
Privacy/Compliance note: Packages include only metadata and anonymized response hashes unless the customer explicitly requests full texts and consents via their support ticket. For enterprise customers with IP-sensitive inputs, we will transmit packages over secure SFTP and limit access to named contacts.
How to request: Open a ticket with subject line: "Request: tenant evidence package — INC-2026-122" or reply to your account team. Include the tenant id (or org id) and desired delivery method.
Timeframe: Evidence packages will be compiled within 72 hours of request receipt; operator-led replays require additional scheduling (1–3 business days).

Customer action choices (decision card)
----
1) Opt in for evidence package (self-serve CSV + hashes).
2) Request operator-led replay (we run replay, provide transcript + verification).
3) Accept a one-time service credit in lieu of replay (CS to propose credit tiers).
4) Request manual verification assistance (account team + SRE triage call).

Draft email / support reply (concise)
----
Subject: Update on your requests during the 2026-11-29 degraded period
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected a partial degradation affecting text generation in us-west-2 on 2026-11-29 03:12–04:35 UTC that may have impacted some of your requests. Immediate mitigation was applied and the service is now validated as recovered. If you’d like, we can provide a tenant evidence package with per-request timelines, integrity hashes, and an operator replay. Reply to this message with the option you prefer and your tenant id.
Thanks for your patience — we understand the disruption.
Sofia Martinez
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Internal quick checklist (for CS + SRE before publishing)
----
- [ ] Verify final monitoring graphs (latency, 5xx, truncation rate) and confirm with SRE.
- [ ] Confirm rollback/patch ID and include in final postmortem.
- [ ] Prepare sample evidence package for one pilot tenant for QA.
- [ ] Draft compensation tiers for account review.
- [ ] Publish micro status update and notify account teams with suggested blurbs.

Open questions / notes to self
----
- Need legal signoff wording for integrity bundle when we include full text outputs (sensitive customers).
- Confirm whether fallback routing caused any per-tenant rate limit consequences (follow up with infra team).
- Decide final public postmortem level of technical detail (ops execs prefer higher level; some enterprise customers will want full timeline).
- Coordinate with product to ensure scheduler test is added to CI (JIRA-OPS-4871).

Appendix: More verbose technical timeline (operator notes)
----
- 03:08 UTC: deploy started (optimizer v2.4.7) to us-west-2 canaries.
- 03:12 UTC: small spike in truncation alerts in canary cluster; automation paged SRE.
- 03:18 UTC: observed divergence in KV cache metrics; partial routing rollbacks initiated to fallback pool.
- 03:28 UTC: mitigation applied (traffic shifted; patch queued).
- 03:55 UTC: patch for guard in eviction path validated in staging; gradual rollout started.
- 04:10 UTC: metrics trending to baseline; verification checks green on majority of tenants.
- 04:35 UTC: rollout complete and automated regression monitor declared recovery.
- 04:50 UTC: begin evidence package generation jobs for impacted tenants (pilot).

Contact and escalation
----
- Incident lead: Ethan Brooks (SRE) — ethan.brooks@redwood.ai
- Customer reliability lead: Sofia Martinez — sofia.martinez@redwood.ai
- Account escalation: Marcus Patel (AM) — marcus.patel@redwood.ai

End of draft.

Notes: keep this lightweight — we want to publish a micro-update quickly, then follow with the full postmortem and evidence flow once packages are available.
